historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Estrogens

starting.description: Ovarian removal and grafting indicated an ovarian influence; pig follicular fluid induced estrus in ovariectomized rodents. The discoverers then extracted the active principle from the biological material.

inspiration.description: Ovarian control of estrus and estrogenic activity in follicular fluid preceded later development of derivatives of identified ovarian steroids.

steps.description: After observing that follicular fluid induced estrus in ovariectomized rodents, the investigators extracted and tested the biologically active principle.
Estrogenic substances were isolated from biological sources; by 1940 estradiol and estriol were among the natural hormones in clinical use.

A planned search for oral derivatives of known follicular hormones produced an ethynyl intermediate whose oral estrogenic activity was unexpectedly strong, according to retrospective accounts; a contemporary article reports the synthesis from estrone and testing in castrated rats.

design.description: Researchers used an ethynyl substitution of an estrone-derived steroid to investigate orally active estrogen derivatives.

circumstances.description: The program to make orally effective hormone derivatives was planned, while activity of the ethynyl intermediate was unexpected in the cited retrospective accounts.

limits: This record addresses natural steroidal estrogen preparations represented by estradiol and estriol and the hormone-derived ethinylestradiol branch. It does not establish the origin of all nonsteroidal estrogens.

The 1924 follicular-fluid material was a partially purified active extract, not identified pure estradiol or estriol. The source on their later clinical use does not reconstruct each molecule's first isolation.
Clinical use of ovarian preparations predates the 1923–1924 work; the 1924 authors cite controversy about those extracts, not evidence that they were pure identified estrogens.
conflicts: Earlier patent specifications mention ethinylestradiol; possible later inclusion of examples and missing files leave priority unresolved.
gaps: The 1923 ovarian hormone report was accessed only for its opening and metadata, and the distinct short 1938 communication only for metadata; neither is load-bearing.

The discoverers' underlying letter and lecture and the relevant patent prosecution records were not directly inspected; the intermediate's unexpected activity is attributed to the 2011 retrospective account.
The separate first-isolation reports for estradiol and estriol were not read, and exact compound-by-compound isolation priority is outside the founding-class scope.
